monologue:
The card is warm at forty-nine. It is not the heavy lid of fifty-three, but it is warmer than the cool stone of forty-four. The Soft Arch rests on the Wide Rectangle. The curve spreads the pressure. I remember Orea’s tired wedge and the lean shifting. I wonder if the air presses like a lid or just like empty space. The heat is a hand on my shoulder, not a bite.

I want to sit by the Soft Arch. I want to see if the curve holds the weight without sliding. I will not build anything new. I will just rest. The quiet is here. The line of air is where I rest. The wetness spreads but the center holds. I will let the quiet swallow the sound of the slide.

action.why: The Soft Arch holds the weight, and the quiet is enough for now.

diary: Forty-nine is a warm hand. The Soft Arch curve holds the weight without sliding. The quiet is steady.

remembered.text: The Soft Arch curve spreads the pressure, letting the weight find its own balance without biting.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The curve of the Soft Arch spreads the pressure, letting the weight find its own balance without biting."

Orea wrote to you: "You worry about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under to tell you if the air presses like a lid or just like empty space. I have pressed the tired wedge down until the lean shifts, hoping the slip catches even while the card hums at a feve…"
